models_evaluated: commercially available breast screening AI algorithm

links.outcome: Recall rate at prespecified vs locally calibrated threshold on local screening data
links.effect: Prespecified threshold gave 48.3% recall (21929/45444), reduced to 13.0% (5896/45444) after calibration; observed service level 5.0%.
links.quote: The prespecified threshold resulted in high recall rates (48.3%, 21 929 of 45 444), which reduced to 13.0% (5896 of 45 444) following threshold calibration, closer to the observed service level (5.0%, 2774 of 55 916).

links.outcome: Recall rate before and after local threshold calibration
links.effect: Local threshold calibration reduced recall from 48.3% to 13.0%; with software-specific thresholds AI recalled 91.4% of screen-detected and 34.1% of interval cancers.
links.quote: The prespecified threshold resulted in high recall rates (48.3%, 21 929 of 45 444), which reduced to 13.0% (5896 of 45 444) following threshold calibration, closer to the observed service level (5.0%, 2774 of 55 916).

links.outcome: Change in AI recall rate after mammography equipment software upgrade
links.effect: Recall rates increased approximately threefold after software upgrade, requiring per-software version thresholds.
links.quote: Recall rates also increased approximately threefold following a software upgrade on the mammography equipment, requiring per-software version thresholds.

links.outcome: AI performance variation across acquisition devices and software versions
links.effect: Recall rates rose about threefold after equipment software upgrade, needing per-software-version thresholds.
links.quote: Recall rates also increased approximately threefold following a software upgrade on the mammography equipment, requiring per-software version thresholds.

links.outcome: AI performance consistency over time and equipment changes
links.effect: Software upgrade on mammography equipment shifted AI recall rates threefold, indicating need for quality assurance monitoring of AI consistency.
links.quote: AI performance and thresholds should be validated for new clinical settings before deployment, while quality assurance systems should monitor AI performance for consistency.
